subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Flywheel: Momentum as a Battery
description: A quick win: understand The Flywheel: Momentum as a Battery.

hook.text: A potter's wheel keeps spinning long after you stop kicking it. The heavy disc stores energy as momentum.

buildup.text: A flywheel is a heavy rotating disc. It absorbs energy when spun up and releases it when slowed down.

discovery.text: Energy stored depends on mass and speed squared. Double the speed and you store four times the energy.

twist.text: Car engines use flywheels to smooth out jerky piston pulses into steady rotation. No flywheel, no smooth idle.

climax.text: Modern flywheels in vacuum chambers spin at 60,000 RPM. They store grid-scale energy without chemicals.

punchline.text: Spin something heavy. You just made a mechanical battery.

quiz.question: How does doubling a flywheel's speed affect its stored energy?
options: Stored energy quadruples because energy scales with speed squared
Stored energy stays the same since mass hasn't changed
